posts.title: Startup and Runtime Smoothness
posts.excerpt: VibeSail starts faster and feels steadier after a Codex /goal performance pass.
posts.author: VibeSail Team

content.text: We used Codex /goal to profile the parts of VibeSail that were making startup and frame pacing feel heavier than they needed to.

items: The game marks the core world ready earlier, then loads wildlife and extra detail in background slices.
Island decoration work now runs in budgeted batches instead of one big startup hit.
Water reflections use an adaptive capture cadence when frames are struggling, then return to full rate when pacing recovers.
The homepage now defers the 3D background until idle time, so the page becomes usable sooner.
Geo scenes prioritize the central city tiles before ambient decoration, keeping the visible world sharp first.

content.text: The videos below show the game loading improvement first, then the homepage loading improvement. In measured runs, homepage DOMContentLoaded dropped from about 772ms to about 117ms, and one geo scene load dropped from about 532ms to about 273ms.

items: https://x.com/NicolaManzini/status/2065051144645132496
https://x.com/NicolaManzini/status/2065051146138345559

posts.title: Meet Boats Around You
posts.excerpt: Tap a nearby boat to see the sailor, flag, boat, and race story behind it.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: A VibeSail boat details popup open beside another sailboat on the water.

content.text: The sea feels better when nearby boats have a story. Now you can click or tap another boat to learn who is sailing beside you.

items: See a sailor's name, flag, boat, speed, heading, and distance.
Guests are still easy to recognize, even without a chosen name.
Named sailors can show daily-race highlights like races, rank, wins, and podiums.
Pirates are marked clearly, with a reminder that your cannons can fight back.

content.text: The popup follows the boat as you move the camera, works on mobile, and keeps the focus on sailing instead of menus.

posts.title: A Bigger World to Sail
posts.excerpt: The sea has a fresh layout with more island variety, clearer routes, and more places to discover.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: A split-screen VibeSail view showing the 3D sailing world beside the top-down island map.

content.text: The VibeSail world now gives you more space to sail, explore, and choose your own route between islands.

items: Islands are spread across a broader sea, so journeys have more open water and better moments of discovery.
New island types give you more distinct places to discover, recognize, and navigate around while sailing.
Cargo ships now sail clearer lanes through the world, making the sea feel more alive without crowding the islands.

posts.title: Daily Mission Routes
posts.excerpt: Cargo missions now refresh by local day, balance nearby and outer-island routes, and keep long route trails easier to read.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: A VibeSail cargo mission route trail leading from the player boat toward distant islands.

content.text: Dock missions now change with the local day, giving each session a fresh set of deliveries while keeping the same calm sailing rhythm.

items: Mission offers now mix short ring routes with longer outer-island routes more deliberately.
Rewards still scale from distance and cargo risk, so fragile and far-away deliveries feel more meaningful.
Long-distance route trails stay visible near the boat instead of fading out too far from the start.
The mission board keeps the same simple accept-and-sail flow while feeling less repetitive from day to day.

posts.title: Race Collisions Removed
posts.excerpt: Daily races now keep ghosts as visual replays only, removing blocker collisions from the active race.
posts.author: VibeSail Team

content.text: We removed collision from daily races. Races still use the regatta start and optional ghost boats, but those ghosts are now visual replays instead of solid blockers.

This came directly from player submissions: racers called out boats getting pushed around marks, mark zones being blocked, and top-three ghosts turning into changing obstacles as the leaderboard moved during the day.
This keeps the race cleaner, reduces frustrating contact at the start, and makes leaderboard runs feel more predictable.

posts.title: Cleaner In-Game Controls
posts.excerpt: The in-game control menu now stays compact while sailing and expands when you need every action.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: VibeSail's expanded in-game control menu over the sailing world.

content.text: The controls on the right side of the screen now take up less space, leaving more of the sea visible while you sail.

items: Keep the menu collapsed for a quieter view of the world.
Expand it whenever you want labeled access to upgrades, the Boat Shop, settings, cannons, the map, multiplayer, and more.
The expanded menu scales to fit shorter screens, so every action remains within reach.

posts.title: Community Feedback Board
posts.excerpt: Share ideas, report problems, and vote on what sailors want next — plus a clearer place to get in touch.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: The VibeSail Feedback community board with public posts, votes, and Top/New sorting.

content.text: VibeSail now has a public Feedback board where sailors can share ideas, report problems, and help decide what matters most.

items: Browse the community board at vibesail.com/feedback.
Vote once per account on any open request — click again to clear your vote.
Sort by Top to see what sailors want most, or New for the latest posts.
Sign in or create an account when you are ready to add your own feedback.
Requests we have already shipped stay on the board with a Done badge, so progress is easy to spot.

content.text: Need something else? The Contact page at vibesail.com/contact gathers our community links and email in one place. Use Feedback for game ideas and bugs, and Contact when you want to reach us directly.

posts.title: A Clearer Way to Set Sail
posts.excerpt: The homepage and public pages got a calmer look: easier to read, easier to tap, and quicker to get on the water.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: Side-by-side before and after of the VibeSail homepage, with the new title card and Set Sail actions on the right.

content.text: We refreshed the homepage and the rest of the public site so the first moment on VibeSail feels clearer and more inviting.
The sailing world is still the star. What changed is how the title, actions, and navigation sit on top of it.

items: The homepage title and short description now sit in a simple dark card, so they stay readable over bright skies and busy docks.
Set Sail leads a tidy stack of actions for the daily race, learning to sail, and the world map, with less clutter and clearer priorities.
The header is easier to scan, with Profile called out and High Sea listed as Beta High Sea under More.
Pages like Feedback, Contact, Profile, and the rest of the site share the same calm look, so moving around VibeSail feels more consistent.

content.text: Nothing about how you sail changed. This is just a cleaner front door into the same open water.

posts.title: Sign In to Log Leaderboard Times
posts.excerpt: You can still race as a guest for practice, but official daily-race and High Sea times now need a signed-in account.
posts.author: VibeSail Team

content.text: VibeSail’s official leaderboards are now account-based. To log a daily-race or High Sea time, sign in or create an account first.

items: Guests can still sail and race for practice — your run just will not be recorded.
Signed-in sailors submit under their profile name, so the board stays fair and easier to follow.
Change your official name anytime on your Profile page.
In multiplayer, only signed-in sailors show a username above their boat.

content.text: If you finish a race while signed out, you will see a clear notice that the time was not recorded, with a quick path to sign in or sign up for the next run.

posts.title: Clearer, Transparent Water
posts.excerpt: The ocean now looks through — transparent water, real refraction, and a visible seabed near shore.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: Before and after of the VibeSail title screen: milky flat water on the left, clear refractive water with a visible seabed on the right.

content.text: The big visual change is the water itself. It is no longer a flat milky sheet — you can look through it.

Near islands and shallow shore, the seabed and rocks show under the surface. Light bends through the waves with refraction and clearer reflections, so the sea feels deeper and more alive from the title screen to open water.

items: Transparent water with refraction instead of a washed-out surface.
Seabed and underwater rocks visible when you sail close to land.
Clearer horizons and richer sun on the water.
Graphics quality in Settings: Low, Medium, or High — same sailing feel, pick the look that fits your device. High keeps the full water detail.

content.text: Head toward an island shoreline and glance down through the water — that visible bottom is the giveaway.

posts.title: Optional Video Ads for Bonus Coins
posts.excerpt: After a Daily Race or cargo mission, you may soon watch a short optional video to double your coins. It will start appearing over the next few days.
posts.author: VibeSail Team
posts.coverAlt: Race Complete panel with +$100 and a Watch an ad to double button marked AD.

content.text: When you finish a Daily Race or a cargo mission, you may see a Watch Ad button to double the coins you just earned.

items: This is optional. Skip it and you keep the normal reward.
Ads never play while you are sailing. They only appear after you finish.
High Sea is unchanged.

content.text: Video ads will start appearing over the next few days as they become available. If you do not see the button yet, that is expected.
